title: August 2026 fresh-intake production - batch H3A-ORB (the Oil Record Book root, released once its amendment chain was held)
note: ONE CARD, AND IT IS THE ROOT H3A REFUSED TO WRITE. AUG-0163 - 'ORB: in detail about the codes' - was held in the H3A run because the only ORB text the corpus held was the 2004 Appendix III from MEPC.117(52), and a later amendment was believed to exist but could not be identified. Publishing the 2004 code list would have been the BMP5 defect exactly: an authoritative base that is stale for the one provision being taught. The blocker is now gone and the card is written from the amendments themselves. WHAT THE HOLD PROTECTED, PRECISELY. MEPC.187(59), in force 1 January 2011, REPLACED Part I sections (A) to (H) in their entirety and Part II section (J). The section LETTERS did not change - which is exactly why a stale answer sounds right and would never have been challenged in the room. The WORDING did: (C) became 'Collection, TRANSFER and disposal of oil residues (sludge)' and gained an item for the quantity collected by manual operation; (D) and (E) changed from 'non-automatic / automatic DISCHARGE' to 'non-automatic / automatic STARTING OF discharge, TRANSFER or disposal'. The common thread is internal transfer, which was previously unrecordable and was how quantities were made to disappear. The same resolution also amended regulation 17.2.3 itself: 'sludge' became the defined term 'oil residue (sludge)' across regs 12.2, 13, 17.2.3, 38.2 and 38.7, and the words 'and other oil residues' were deleted from 17.2.3. Section (I) was NOT replaced. RQ-A2 CLOSED IN THE SAME PASS. MEPC.314(74), in force 1 October 2020, was raised as an open acquisition item by H3A and is now held and used. It adds regulation 1.39 defining an Electronic Record Book as 'a device or system, APPROVED BY THE ADMINISTRATION, used to electronically record the required entries...in lieu of a hard copy record book', amends regs 17.1 and 36.1 to permit it 'taking into account the Guidelines developed by the Organization', and inserts 'or group of electronic entries' into the signature rule. Without it the card could only have hedged on electronic ORBs; with it the card can state the one word that decides the answer, which is APPROVED. NO DUPLICATE, BUT THE FIRST SWEEP THAT SAID SO WAS WRONG. No card carries the Oil Record Book in its title and 75 mention it at baseline ebabe00, both reproducible. The claim that ZERO carried any section-code structure was FALSE: QB1_supplementary#q6 carried all nine Part I letters in its CE tip in the pre-2011 wording, and the sweep pattern could not see them because it was written for the shape 'section (C)' while that card writes 'A = Ballasting of fuel oil tanks'. The pattern /\bA\b\s*=\s*Ballast/i returns it. The card is corrected under CORR-ORB-02 and the new card remains the only one that TEACHES the ORB; the duplicate finding stands, the reasoning that produced it did not. The four heaviest mentioners were read in full - QB5_B#q1 (CE handover), QB1_F#q2 (MARPOL documents), QB1_supplementary#q6 (IOPP survey checklist) and QB3_F#q8 (OWS failure) - and each uses the ORB as an item in a list or a consequence in a scenario. None teaches it. EXAMINER ATTRIBUTION IS DIFFERENT HERE. Unlike every H2 and H3A card, AUG-0163 is INDIVIDUALLY_ATTRIBUTED: the candidate wrote 'Internal:' above it and the internal examiner was Senthil, resolved through ROLE_MARKER_SOLE_HOLDER. The name follows from that seat having a sole holder, which is an inference over role evidence rather than a name the candidate wrote, and the card now says so in those terms. The examiner-relationship total is nevertheless unchanged at 958 - the index harvests names from the CE-tip and header surfaces rather than from the deep-dive block where this one sits - and that is reported as measured rather than assumed. DIGEST REPINNED. The card's post-edit digest was recomputed after the independent review's round-2 findings were applied to it: the reg. 36.5/36.6/36.7/36.9 paragraphs, the '(All Ships)' Appendix III form-header disarm, the softened examiner attribution and the narrowed enforcement sentence. The digest recorded before those edits was c8b58096eff2ce7551f4f02432830970c96d90ecac4b381c92e2724d1e0fddbd and is superseded by e78d49c62024af98d9f33f3701174766e98e3e348938185e915cccb39013a5e2.
